provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — first-execution of an unsigned executable masquerading as a document from a user-writable path is detectable via process-creation telemetry, image-path and icon/extension-mismatch heuristics
medium — filenames with excessive length or embedded double extensions before .exe are detectable via file-name pattern analytics on process creation and file writes
medium — executables carrying document icons and dropping/opening a decoy doc are detectable via resource/icon inspection and process-lineage (an .exe spawning a document viewer at first run)

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation of .lnk files in the Startup folder is directly observable via file-creation telemetry (Sysmon EID 11) on a well-known persistence path; NetworkBoosterUtilities.lnk is an actor-specific artifact

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — writes to HKCU...\Run and startup-folder entries are directly observable via registry-modification and file-creation auditing (Sysmon EID 13/11)
medium — PyInstaller-bundled executables and Python-runtime child processes are detectable via process telemetry, but resemble legitimate packaged Python apps without additional context

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe spawned by an unusual parent implant process is detectable via process-lineage analytics, but command-shell use is common and needs context
medium — keylogging is stealthy at runtime, but the keystroke-log output directory/files and the dedicated keylogger binary are detectable via file-creation and process telemetry

medium — screen-capture APIs are hard to catch directly, but the resulting timestamped PNG artifacts and periodic capture behavior are detectable via file-write telemetry in the implant's working directory

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to Chrome's Login Data SQLite store by a non-browser process is detectable via file-access and process telemetry, though it requires targeted instrumentation
medium — bulk enumeration/reads of many office documents by an unusual process are detectable via file-access analytics and staging correlation, but blend with normal user activity
medium — regular, periodic collection bursts (screenshots/logs on a timer) are detectable via file-creation cadence analytics in the implant working directory
medium — programmatic enumeration of removable-drive contents shortly after device insertion is detectable via WMI-query and file-access telemetry correlated with USB device-connect events
medium — WMI queries against Win32_USB/DiskDrive classes from a non-management process are detectable via WMI-activity and command-line telemetry
medium — WMI queries for AntiVirusProduct/SecurityCenter2 and disk devices from an untrusted process are detectable via WMI operational logging and process telemetry
medium — enumeration of security products via WMI/registry by an unknown process is detectable via WMI and command-line telemetry and is a meaningful early-stage signal

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: high — execution of rar.exe with password-protection flags creating archives of document collections in a staging directory is a high-fidelity, detectable pre-exfiltration signal via process command-line and file-write telemetry
medium — accumulation of collection artifacts in a hidden/fixed staging directory is detectable via file-creation clustering; the HPFusionManagerDell directory name is an actor-specific artifact
medium — beaconing HTTP POSTs to the specific persona C2 domains with the distinctive URI structure are detectable via proxy/DNS and network telemetry when the domains/paths are known
medium — implant processes writing and launching new executables fetched from C2 are detectable via file-write + process-creation lineage, especially tied to the known C2 domains
medium — base64-encoded C2 parameters in HTTP requests are detectable via network/proxy content analytics when combined with the known URI patterns
medium — outbound uploads to the known persona C2 domains, sized/paced unusually, are detectable via network egress and DLP telemetry once C2 is identified

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — actor-controlled social-media personas are off-victim and not endpoint-observable; intel/brand-monitoring and takedown candidate
low — domain registration occurs off-victim; hunt/intel candidate via WHOIS/registration-pattern pivoting and C2 domain blocklisting
low — acquisition/standing-up of cloud web-service C2 is off-victim; the downstream Firebase traffic is where limited detection lands
low — capability development is off-victim; intel/tracking candidate via code-lineage and family clustering
low — staging on actor-owned infrastructure is off-victim; hunt candidate via URL/domain blocklisting and web telemetry for the specific download paths
low — off-platform social-engineering over third-party services is not enterprise-log-observable; awareness/policy and mobile-threat-defense candidate
low — link delivery occurs on social/video platforms off-victim; the endpoint signal is the subsequent APK install, not the link
low — user click on an external link is largely off the defended endpoint; web-proxy/DNS telemetry to the specific persona domains is the only weak signal
low — microphone/call recording on mobile is opaque to enterprise logging; mobile-threat-defense and permission-audit candidate
low — single OS/version queries are ubiquitous and low-signal; hunt-only in tight process-lineage context
low — retrieval of computer/user name is ubiquitous; low-signal hunt-only
low — file enumeration is high-volume and largely legitimate; hunt-only within a recon-burst window
low — Firebase C2 rides legitimate Google infrastructure and blends with normal mobile traffic; mobile-threat-defense candidate, weakly detectable in enterprise logs
low — vendor-specific notification suppression on mobile is not enterprise-log-observable; mobile-threat-defense and permission-audit candidate
low — on-device evasion logic is not enterprise-observable; relevant to malware-analysis tradecraft rather than production detection
low — obfuscation is an intrinsic sample property observed in analysis rather than a runtime host signal; YARA/static-analysis candidate
low — in-process decoding leaves little discrete host signal; analysis-time indicator rather than a production detection
low — webshells on the actor's own infrastructure are off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via infrastructure fingerprinting
